steps.instruction: Import the express, multer, and path modules using require statements.
steps.hint: Use require('module-name') to import each module. You'll need three separate require statements.

steps.title: Configure multer storage for file uploads
steps.instruction: Create a multer disk storage configuration object that specifies where uploaded files should be stored and how they should be named.
steps.hint: Use multer.diskStorage() with an options object containing destination and filename functions. The destination function should use path.join() to create an 'uploads' directory, and filename should return the original file name.
steps.expectedOutcome: A storage configuration object is created that will handle where uploaded files are saved and what they're named.
successCriteria: A multer.diskStorage() configuration is defined with destination and filename functions.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully configured multer storage. This tells multer where to save uploaded files and how to name them.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've included both destination and filename functions in your storage configuration.
steps.feedbackWrong: The storage configuration isn't quite right. Remember to use multer.diskStorage() with an object containing destination and filename functions.

steps.title: Create multer upload middleware with file filter
steps.instruction: Create a multer instance named 'upload' that uses the storage configuration and includes a file filter function to accept only image files (jpeg, png, gif).
steps.hint: Call multer() with an object containing 'storage' and 'fileFilter' properties. The fileFilter function should check the file's mimetype.
steps.expectedOutcome: A multer instance named 'upload' is created with storage configuration and a file filter that validates image files.
successCriteria: The 'upload' constant is defined using multer() with both storage and fileFilter properties. The fileFilter function checks mimetype for image formats.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the multer upload middleware with file validation. This will ensure only image files are accepted during upload.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your fileFilter function properly validates image mimetypes (jpeg, png, gif) and calls the callback correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The upload middleware isn't configured correctly. Make sure to create a multer instance with both storage and fileFilter properties.

steps.title: Define the upload endpoint route
steps.instruction: Create a POST route at '/upload' that uses the multer upload middleware you configured earlier.
steps.hint: Use app.post() with the route path and the upload middleware as the first argument in the callback chain.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Express app will have a POST route at '/upload' ready to handle file uploads.
successCriteria: A POST route is defined at '/upload' and uses the multer upload middleware.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the upload endpoint route.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using app.post() with '/upload' and the upload middleware.
steps.feedbackWrong: The route isn't defined correctly. Check the syntax for creating a POST route with middleware.

steps.title: Add validation for file existence in the route handler
steps.instruction: Inside the upload endpoint route handler, add a conditional check to verify if req.file exists. If it doesn't exist, return a 400 status with a JSON error message: 'No file uploaded'.
steps.hint: Use an if statement to check if req.file is falsy (undefined or null). If so, use res.status(400).json({ error: 'No file uploaded' }) and return to end the request.
steps.expectedOutcome: The route handler now validates that a file was uploaded before proceeding, returning an appropriate error response if not.
successCriteria: The route handler includes an if statement checking if req.file exists, returns a 400 status with JSON error message when missing.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added validation to check if a file was uploaded, providing clear feedback when it's missing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some validation, but make sure to check if req.file exists and return the proper 400 status with JSON error message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validation for file existence isn't implemented correctly. Add an if statement to check req.file and return an error response when it's missing.

steps.title: Add file size validation in the route handler
steps.instruction: Inside the /upload route handler, add validation to check if the uploaded file exceeds 5MB (5 * 1024 * 1024 bytes). If it does, return a 400 status with an error message.
steps.hint: Check req.file.size against the maximum size. Use res.status(400).json() to send the error response.
steps.expectedOutcome: The route handler will now reject files larger than 5MB with a proper error response.
successCriteria: File size validation is implemented with a 5MB limit and returns a 400 status with an error message when exceeded.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added file size validation to prevent oversized uploads.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some validation, but make sure to check the exact size limit (5MB) and return the proper error response.
steps.feedbackWrong: The size validation isn't implemented correctly. Check the file size and return a 400 status with an error message when it exceeds the limit.

steps.title: Add file type validation in the route handler
steps.instruction: Inside the /upload route handler, add validation to check if the uploaded file has an allowed MIME type (e.g., 'image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'application/pdf'). If the file type is not allowed, return a 400 response with an appropriate error message.
steps.hint: You can access the file's MIME type via req.file.mimetype. Create an array of allowed MIME types and use includes() to check if the uploaded file's type is in that array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The route handler now includes validation for allowed file types, rejecting files with unsupported MIME types with a 400 error response.
successCriteria: The route handler contains a check for allowed MIME types using an array and includes(), and returns a 400 response with an error message when the file type is invalid.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added file type validation to ensure only allowed file types are accepted.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some validation, but make sure to check the file's MIME type against an array of allowed types and return a 400 response with an error message if it's invalid.
steps.feedbackWrong: The file type validation is missing or incorrect. Ensure you're checking req.file.mimetype against an array of allowed MIME types and returning a proper error response.

steps.title: Handle successful upload response
steps.instruction: In the upload route handler, after all validation passes, return a JSON response with a success message and the uploaded file's details.
steps.hint: Use res.json() to send a JSON response. Include properties like 'message' and 'file' in the response object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The route handler now returns a JSON response when validation passes, confirming the upload was successful and providing file information.
successCriteria: The upload endpoint returns a JSON response with a success message and file details after all validation passes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the success response. The endpoint now properly confirms uploads with file details.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your response includes both a 'message' property and a 'file' property with the uploaded file's details.
steps.feedbackWrong: The upload endpoint doesn't yet return a proper success response. After validation, use res.json() to send a JSON object with success message and file details.

steps.title: Start the Express server
steps.instruction: Make the Express application listen for incoming requests on port 3000 and log a startup message.
steps.hint: Use the app.listen() method with the port number and a callback function that logs a message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will be running and ready to handle file upload requests at http://localhost:3000/upload.
successCriteria: The app.listen() method is called with port 3000 and a callback that logs a startup message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! Your server is now running and ready to accept file uploads.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the server, but make sure to include a callback that logs a message when it's running.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server isn't started yet. Use app.listen() with port 3000 and a callback.
